title: Q4 Inference Runway & Security Readiness
summary: Quarterly health check focusing on usage trends, a recent cost spike in November, reliability incidents around a 99.5% tail latency event, and security readiness for an upcoming audit. Redwood proposed batching and prefix caching adjustments, a short dedicated pilot for peak windows, and timeline for SOC2 artifacts. Customer wants clearer cost forecasts and an SLA playbook. Agreement to run a 2-week cost/stability pilot next month and share security package and benchmarks.

Dedicated capacity vs hosted bursts for peak windows

Roadmap: pilot timeline and success metrics

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (NexaHealth VP Eng), Meera Patel (NexaHealth SRE Lead), Samir Gupta (NexaHealth CFO)

Summary (auto): QBR-style check-in. Reviewed recent cost spike, reliability incident on 11/18, and security readiness for audit. Agreed pilots and deliverables.

[00:00] Alex Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we're gonna run through platform health, costs, and the security checklist you asked for. Jordan, Mei-- Meera, you said you'd share the incident notes up front, thanks.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Yeah hi, thanks Alex. Real quick context for folks, traffic spiked in late Nov when we shipped the new conversational routing, so tokens doubled for a few hours and that drove up cost. We also saw a tail latency issue that surfaced.
[00:34] Priya Shah: Got it. We pulled the traces for the 11/18 window and saw some concurrent KV cache misses which increased runtime, looked like a cold-spot in the prefix cache, and a couple of requests hit long sequence lengths.
[00:52] Meera Patel: Right, the prefix cache warmed slower than expected during the burst. Our on-call noted 504-ish downstream timeouts, but there wasn't a full outage. Just high tail latency.
[01:08] Alex Ramos: Understood. Samir, from a finance angle, was the cost jump within your forecast band or outside?
[01:15] Samir Gupta: Outside; it pushed our monthly over budget by ~12%. We need predictability — the CFO math doesn't like surprises. We want a guardrail and a plan to avoid this repeating.
[01:30] Priya Shah: Two levers we've seen work: short dedicated capacity windows for predictable peaks, or aggressive batching + prefix caching tweaks to lower per-token cost without always reserving capacity. There's tradeoffs on latency.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: Latency's important for UX—can't accept degraded real-time response. But we could accept slightly higher median if tail is fixed.
[01:58] Meera Patel: Also want to confirm data residency and KMS flow for forwarded logs and cache keys. Our compliance team will ask for KMS control and encrypted-at-rest proof.
[02:12] Alex Ramos: Yes, we can provide the KMS integration doc and audit logs. I'll attach the security package. Priya, can you run through the performance changes you recommend for the pilot?
[02:25] Priya Shah: Sure. Short plan: 1) Increase prefix cache size and reduce TTL miss rate by pre-warming common prompts, 2) Tune batch size and max-latency thresholds—use adaptive batching with a 30ms micro-window for low-latency routes, 3) For predictable peaks, spin up a small Dedicated pool for 2–4 hours windows to handle headroom and give you flat unit costs.
[02:56] Jordan Lee: That Dedicated pool—what's the delta on price? Is it a big commitment?
[03:03] Alex Ramos: For pilots, we offer a short-term reserved slice with hourly billing and a small commitment. We'll send a pricing delta matrix later today. For long term we can do reserved monthly contracts.
[03:18] Samir Gupta: We need the worksheet to show TCO across scenarios — hosted with autoscale, hosted with batching, dedicated pilot. Also any quantization or model variant cost impacts.
[03:34] Priya Shah: We'll include model-variant recommendations and quantization guidance; note that very aggressive quantization can affect quality—so we'll include a quality delta table per workload.
[03:46] Meera Patel: On security, checklist items: SOC2 readiness, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC for model access, KMS/HSM keys, audit logs retention. Who owns the SOC2 artifacts?
[03:58] Alex Ramos: Redwood provides the SOC2 attestations and we can share the SOC2 Type II report; we'll also provide the mapping doc for controls, and the technical artifacts for KMS and audit logs.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: Good. Also need network flows for Private deployment if we go that route — VPC peering or on-prem. We might need an on-prem package for PHI use cases.
[04:24] Priya Shah: We have both VPC and on-prem playbooks. For PHI we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS. That's more work but hits compliance points.
[04:37] (background) Meera Patel: [quiet] We will check legal on the PHI clause.
[04:42] Alex Ramos: Ok, action items: I'll send the security package and SOC2 artifacts today, Priya will send the caching/batching doc, and we'll build the pilot runbook.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: Can we get an example runbook? Steps to onboard the dedicated pool, sample traffic hooks, rollback steps?
[05:00] Priya Shah: Yes, pilot runbook will include onboarding steps, health checks, tracing hooks, automated fallback to hosted variants, and how to cut over.
[05:12] Samir Gupta: Also please highlight the SLA delta if we use dedicated vs hosted — we need uptime and latency SLO expectations for both.
[05:22] Alex Ramos: We'll include SLA language and historical percentiles we've observed across customers.
[05:28] Jordan Lee: Quick Q on the tail latency: do you think it's a kernel-level optimization or request pattern problem?
[05:35] Priya Shah: From the traces it's request pattern — unusually long sequences plus cache misses. But we will also propose a couple of runtime patches; one is an attention kernel switch that reduces latency for long sequences; low-risk but needs testing.
[05:52] Meera Patel: Timeline for those runtime patches?
[05:56] Priya Shah: We can test in staging within two weeks, but won't push to prod until pilot sign-off.
[06:04] Alex Ramos: Can we talk about metrics for pilot success? Jordan?
[06:09] Jordan Lee: KPIs: 1) Monthly cost delta <= 5% vs baseline, 2) 99th percentile latency under 450ms for interactive routes, 3) No more than one P2 incident during pilot.
[06:25] Samir Gupta: Add a finance KPI: cost predictability measure — variance under 3% during pilot.
[06:33] Alex Ramos: Noted. We'll bake those into the runbook.
[06:38] [10:12] Priya Shah: (fast forward) I pulled a short sample of token-level billing for your top 10 routes — I recommend per-route batching profiles, and the top offender is the long-context summarization route, which we can shard to a cheaper model for non-real-time use.
[10:35] Jordan Lee: Hmm okay, we can move the batch summarization to an async flow. That should reduce peak synchronous load.
[10:41] Meera Patel: That might solve a lot — will coordinate with product.
[10:46] Alex Ramos: Also a quick note on competitors — you mentioned Atlas AI earlier. Their pricing is a bit lower on large-context but they don't give the same observability or on-prem options. We'll include a short competitor comparison doc.
[11:03] Jordan Lee: Helpful. We have a procurement review scheduled mid-January; want to have the pilot and security docs in hand by then.
[11:10] Alex Ramos: We'll target sending docs by 2026-12-10 and a finalized pilot scope by 2026-12-20.
[11:18] [23:00] Meera Patel: One more technical question: how do you handle KV-cache keys for PII? We need the cache not to preserve raw PII.
[23:08] Priya Shah: Good point. We recommend hashing cache keys client-side and not storing any raw PII in logs. We'll include the recommended hashing scheme and retention policy in the security pack.
[23:22] Jordan Lee: Can you also show us the log redaction flow? Our auditors will ask.
[23:27] Alex Ramos: Yep, redaction flow plus retention windows, and sample audit logs.
[23:33] [34:12] Samir Gupta: Just to push on billing again — if we do a dedicated slice for peak hours, can you provide an example monthly forecast with varying peak-day counts? We need scenario A/B/C for execs.
[34:23] Priya Shah: We'll produce three scenarios: conservative (2 peak days/week), moderate (5 peak days/week), aggressive (daily peaks). Each will show cost per token and net expense vs hosted.
[34:36] Alex Ramos: We'll also show a breakeven graph — when dedicated becomes cheaper given your peak frequency.
[34:41] Jordan Lee: Great.
[34:44] [48:05] Meera Patel: Any blockers from Redwood side to run the pilot? Network or access we should prep?
[48:12] Priya Shah: We'll need a service account with minimal IAM permissions for pilot telemetry and a temporary VPC peering config if you want dedicated in your region. We'll provide the exact checklist.
[48:24] Meera Patel: Ok will get security to provision.
[48:28] Alex Ramos: Final recap — Redwood will: 1) send security package & SOC2 artifacts (today), 2) send batching/caching suggestions (by 12/13), 3) send cost model and pricing delta (by 12/16), 4) provide pilot runbook and scenario forecasts (by 12/20). NexaHealth will: 1) share SRE postmortem and traffic patterns (by 12/12), 2) confirm pilot KPIs and budget (by 12/20).
[48:58] Jordan Lee: Sounds good.
[49:01] Samir Gupta: One small ask — include an easy one-page brief suitable for our CFO deck.
[49:06] Alex Ramos: Will do.
[49:09] Meera Patel: Thanks all.
[49:12] Alex Ramos: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and lock dates.
[57:30] (call ends)

References and links mentioned: Security package: (link shared in chat), Pilot runbook template (link to doc), Cost worksheet (link to spreadsheet).

Notes on transcript quality: Some proper nouns and acronyms were auto-transcribed as phonetically similar words ("K V cash" for KV cache). Occasional timestamp drift.
